messages:
Priya Patel: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands  putting process Qs here (release cadence, oncall, quality bars, SLAs). We’ll answer during the live Q&A in ~15m and drop notes after. Keep Qs short.

Ben Ortiz: Are we shifting to a safer biweekly cadence? engineering bandwidth feels tight.

Priya Patel: Short answer: hosted API stays weekly as the default. We'll formalize a "stability window" policy: teams can opt into a 2-week train for big infra work or compliance freezes, with a 7d notice and EngOps approval.

Lina Wang: For weekly trains, what's the agreed canary plan? we need clear steps so infra can prepare.

Priya Patel: Canary plan: stage to 2% for 15m smoke, expand to 20% for 45m if stable, then progressive ramp. Abort triggers: error-rate increase >1.0% absolute OR p99 latency increase >25% sustained >3m OR external dependency error spike. We'll publish a runbook with exact metrics and a rollback playbook.

Samir Gupta: Rollback criteria sound stricter than before. Are perf regressions handled differently?

Priya Patel: Perf regressions: small regressions (<10% p95) go to mitigation tickets and monitored; large regressions (>15% p95 or p99 jump) trigger immediate abort. Runtime-touch PRs must include a perf-smoke result in the PR description. Full perf suite is still async but promotion to heavy-pools is blocked on failing core perf checks.

Ben Ortiz: Oncall rotation: any plan to ease burden? 1-week is rough for some teams.

Priya Patel: We're piloting 2-week rotations for SRE teams next month with paid handover overlap and a documented shadowing flow. Product/runtime teams keep 1-week for now; will re-evaluate after the pilot. Also adding "one swap" grace per quarter.

Lina Wang: Quality bars: will we mandate coverage % or rely on code review? some libs are under-tested.

Priya Patel: No single mandatory coverage across the org. Instead: repo-level targets set in the README (recommended: libs 60%, services 80%). Mandatory checks: CI green, unit tests for new code, lint & types. Add an entry in PR template for testing rationale if below target.

Samir Gupta: SLA specifics for Dedicated customers? pro-rated credits?

Priya Patel: Hosted public SLA: 99.9. Dedicated customers can buy 99.95 with reserved capacity + contract terms. Credits are prorated per contract window; legal is drafting sample calculations and we'll post an SLA matrix with worked examples.

incident-bot: incident-bot: Canary deployment kicked off for train/2026-06-21 (build: 2026.06.21-9a3c).

Priya Patel: Action items: I'll publish a 1-page FAQ + the canary runbook by EOD Fri. @Samir to update PR template with perf-smoke snippet. @Lina to collect repo README coverage targets. We'll link docs in #eng-docs after the live Q&A.

Ben Ortiz: Thanks thumbsup

Priya Patel: Thanks all  recording + notes will be up after the session.
